title: Patch: `classify --base origin/main` on a branch behind main reads only the branch's own change, not main's newer commits in reverse
thread:
**Issue #4849 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #4849: Patch: `classify --base origin/main` on a branch behind main reads only the branch's own change, not main's newer commits in reverse
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

`cargo jackioh classify` compares two trees: `git diff --no-renames --name-only <base> <head>` (`crates/tools/src/classify.rs:1382`), and it reads the base's side and fragments at `base` itself (`:1392`, `:1425`). When the base is not an ancestor of the head, everything `main` merged since the branch forked is diffed in reverse and attributed to the branch.

An empty branch forked just before a card patch, checked against `main` at that patch (real commits, run read-only with the built binary):

```
$ jackioh classify --base d96d7a8 --head d96d7a8^
classify: Cards, micro
  wording only: core-002, core-021, meditative-018, … (12 families)      # the branch changed nothing
$ jackioh classify --base cd50525 --head cd50525^ --claims
--claims needs --parent-bin: stage 1 left script:stinkyscape-009, play-code unchecked    (exit 1)
$ jackioh classify --base 13ea81e --head 13ea81e^ --claims
--claims needs --parent-bin: stage 1 left script:classicplus-019-5, script:meditative-048, … (exit 1)
```

CI is not affected: `rust (classify)` passes the merge commit's first parent, which is an ancestor. The people and agents who follow the documented pre-push step are: on any branch that is behind `main`, the check fails or names cards the branch never touched.

### What should happen

`CLAUDE.md` (CI): "Run `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` before pushing", and in the same section "merge `main` into a pull request only when GitHub shows a conflict". `.github/pull_request_template.md:40` and `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md:209` give the same command. `--base` is documented as "The commit the change starts from (a pull request's base)". A branch that is behind `main`, checked the documented way, should be told what *it* changes.

### How to reproduce

The three commands above, against this repository. There is no test in the audit's file for this one: `classify` reads the compile-time repository root and cannot be pointed at a fixture repository.

### Where

CI, deploys or tooling: `crates/tools/src/classify.rs` (`run`, and the readers of `base`).

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- In `classify::run`, when `base` is not an ancestor of `head`, diff from `git merge-base base head` (and read the base's side and its fragments there). That is what a pull request's change is, and it leaves CI's call, whose base is already an ancestor, exactly as it is. The alternative is to fail with a message that says to bring the branch up to date, but that contradicts the instruction not to merge `main` without a conflict.
- `--parent-bin`: a parent build made at `origin/main` is then not the build of the merge base. Say in the error message or the README which build stage 2 wants, or have `--claims` name the merge base it used so the caller can build that.
- `changed.rs` and `technical.rs` already use first parents; check they need nothing.
- A test needs `classify` to take a repository root (as `spec` takes `--root`); adding that option, used only by the test, is the cleanest way to hold this, and would also let the other gates' checks be tested on fixtures.
- No ruling or README states tree-against-tree semantics as intended for a diverged base (R1365000, R1370000).
- Update `crates/tools/README.md` and the three places that print the command if its meaning or its options change.

Found by an audit of the project's own gates (`crates/tools`); reproduced with the built binary and the code read before filing.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45526399176)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`cargo jackioh classify --base <rev>` reads the branch's own change even when `<rev>` is behind the head: stage 1 diffs from `git merge-base base head` instead of `base`, and the base side, its fragments, and stage 2's expected parent build all mean that merge base. A `--root` option (test-only, copied from `spec --root`) lets tests point `classify` at a fixture repository. No new ruling: this is tooling semantics, not a game rule, so the two governing notes are amended in place.

## Files to touch

| Path | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/tools/src/classify.rs` | change | `Args`: add `root`; new `effective_base()` and extracted `load()`; `run()` uses them; diverged-base stderr note; `--parent-bin` error names the merge-base build; `Report` gains `merge_base`; doc comments; tests |
| `crates/tools/README.md` | change | `classify` row: add `[--root <dir>]`, describe merge-base reading and which build stage 2 wants |
| `spec/rulings/R1365000.md` | change | One sentence: the change is read between the merge base and the head |
| `spec/rulings/R1370000.md` | change | One sentence: stage 2 runs against the merge base's build |
| `spec/pending/4849.md` | new | The §11 paragraph for this issue (format per `spec/README.md` and a sibling pending file) |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/tools/src/changed.rs`, `crates/tools/src/technical.rs`, `crates/tools/src/claims.rs`, `crates/tools/src/main.rs`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/pull_request_template.md`, `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` (their printed invocations stay correct; the README row carries the semantics). Governing spec: R1365000, R1370000 (no new R number; no README states tree-against-tree semantics for a diverged base today).

## Steps

1. In `crates/tools/src/classify.rs`, add to `Args` (after `head`, copying `spec::Args` in `crates/tools/src/spec.rs:60-63`): `/// The repository root (default: the workspace this binary was built from, as every other command reads it). #[arg(long)] pub root: Option<PathBuf>`. Import `repo_root` (already imports `crate::patches::{git, repo_root}` at `:44`; confirm and reuse).
2. Add `fn effective_base(root: &Path, base: &str, head: &str) -> Result<String>`: run `git merge-base <base> <head>` via the existing `git()` helper, return its trimmed stdout; if that fails (only possible with unrelated histories, since `run()` already resolved both revs), return `base.to_string()`, preserving today's behavior. Do not add an ancestry check: when `base` is an ancestor, merge-base equals `base`, so CI's call is byte-identical.
3. Extract `run()`'s lines `:1381-1393` into `fn load(root: &Path, base: &str, head: &str) -> Result<Loaded>` with `struct Loaded { effective: String, files: Vec<FileChange>, before: Side, after: Side }`, where `effective = effective_base(...)` and the diff, `show()`, and `side_at()` calls all use `effective`. `run()` becomes: `let root = args.root.unwrap_or_else(repo_root);` then `let loaded = load(&root, &base, &head)?`.
4. In `run()`, after loading, if `loaded.effective != base`, print to stderr exactly: `classify: <base> is not an ancestor of <head>; reading the branch's change from their merge base <effective>`. Read both fragment sets as `fragments_at(&root, &head)` and `fragments_at(&root, &loaded.effective)` (replacing `:1424-1425`).
5. Change the `:1416-1420` bail to name the required build: `--claims needs --parent-bin (<that build's jackioh>): stage 1 left <unchecked> unchecked; stage 2 wants a build of the merge base <effective>`. Update the `parent_bin` field doc (`:141-142`) and `SelfplaySide::Base` doc (`:167`) from "the base's build" to "the merge base's build".
6. Add `merge_base: String` to `Report` (`:182-190`), set to `loaded.effective`. Additive field; CI's `jq` reads `.labels`, `.problems`, `.unchecked` only. First check no test asserts exact `Report` JSON (search `merge_base\|Report {` under `crates/tools`).
7. Update the `classify` row of `crates/tools/README.md` (acceptance test `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` requires the new `--root` flag to appear there): command cell becomes `classify --base <rev> [--head <rev>] [--root <dir>] [--parent-bin <path>] [--json] [--claims] [--selfplay-side head\|base] [--selfplay-dir <dir>]`; description states it reads the branch's change from `git merge-base` of base and head, and that `--parent-bin` must be that merge base's build.
8. Amend `spec/rulings/R1365000.md`: the "reads a change between two commits" sentence becomes "reads a change between a base and a head, from their merge base (`git merge-base`), so a base behind the head still classifies only the branch". Amend `spec/rulings/R1370000.md`: "Stage 2 runs against main's build of the base commit" becomes "against the merge base's build". Create `spec/pending/4849.md` with the §11 paragraph for this issue.
9. Verify `changed.rs` (`since_base` diffs the merge commit's first parent to HEAD) and `technical.rs` (each commit vs its first parent) need nothing; change neither.

## Tests

- `crates/tools/src/classify.rs`, `fn r1365000_diverged_base_reads_the_branch_from_the_merge_base`: copy the `TempRepo` helper from `crates/tools/src/changed.rs` tests (init `-b main`, `write`, `commit` with `user.name/email` `-c` flags). Fixture: commit A with a catalog of `core-001`/`core-002` and one script (reuse `changed.rs` tests' `entry`/`catalog`/`script` builders); commit B on main changing `core-002`'s script; branch off A committing C changing `core-001`'s script. Assert `effective_base(root, B, C) == A`; assert the file list between `A` and `C` names only `core-001`'s script while `B..C` also names `core-002`'s (locks the reported bug shape); assert `read_diff` over `Side::of_catalog` sides built from the `A`/`C` catalogs names only family `core-001`.
- `crates/tools/src/classify.rs`, `fn r1365000_an_ancestor_base_is_used_unchanged`: linear fixture; assert `effective_base(root, B, C) == B` and no stderr contract is needed.
- Keep tests at the git-plus-`read_diff` level (no `side_at`, which would need engine config fixtures); existing `r1365000_*`/`r2499000_*` tests already cover classification from `Side`s.
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-tools classify`, then `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Diverged base: diff, base side, and base fragments all read at the merge base; only the branch's families reported.
- [ ] Ancestor base (CI's call): behavior unchanged, no stderr note.
- [ ] `--claims` failure and JSON report name the merge base whose build stage 2 wants.
- [ ] `--root` points `classify` at a fixture repo; default is the build workspace.
- [ ] `changed.rs`, `technical.rs` verified untouched and unaffected.
- [ ] README row, both ruling notes, and `spec/pending/4849.md` updated; the three printed invocations (PR template, `ADDING_CARDS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) confirmed still correct and unedited.
- [ ] All tests and checks above pass.

## Risks

- Shallow or partial checkouts lacking either commit: `rev()` already fails there today, before merge-base runs; no new failure mode. Unrelated histories fall back to `base` (today's behavior), not a new error.
- The always-present JSON `merge_base` field: additive, but confirm no golden file or test pins `Report`'s exact shape.
- Amending ruling notes must keep `id`/filename match, unique ids, and resolvable `[[…]]` links or `spec check` fails; no new `R` token is introduced, so no new proving-test obligation arises.

## Open questions

None blocking. One naming choice the reviewer may correct: the JSON field is `merge_base`; if the project prefers `base` or `effective_base`, it is a one-line rename in `Report` and step 5's message.
````
